thread.title: Typhoon Kalmaegi Causes Devastation in the Philippines
thread.title_full: Typhoon Kalmaegi Causes Devastation in the Philippines

author: Associated Press Television News
title: Typhoon Kalmaegi Causes Devastation in the Philippines
text:
• Typhoon Kalmaegi has resulted in at least 114 deaths in the Philippines.
• 127 people are reported missing, primarily in the central province of Cebu.
• Most fatalities were due to drowning in flash floods.
• The typhoon has been declared the deadliest natural disaster of the year for the Philippines.
• Nearly 2 million people were affected by the typhoon, with over 560,000 displaced.
• Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. declared a state of emergency on November 6, 2025.
• The declaration allows for faster disbursement of emergency funds and prevents food hoarding.
• Kalmaegi has moved into the South China Sea and is approaching Vietnam.
• Ho Chi Minh City is at risk of severe flooding due to high tides and expected heavy rainfall.
• Cebu experienced about one-and-a-half months' worth of rainfall in just one day.
• At least 71 deaths occurred in Cebu, with 65 others reported missing and 69 injured.
• 62 additional people are reported missing in Negros Occidental, near Cebu.
• Cebu was still recovering from a 6.9 magnitude earthquake that occurred on September 30, 2025.
• The Philippines is prone to about 20 typhoons and storms annually, along with earthquakes and volcanic activity.
